caption: ERP and EIRP as dB bookkeeping from transmitter to antenna. Section 1 walks the pool's repeater example (E9A02): 150 watts out, minus 2 dB of feed line loss, minus 2.2 dB of duplexer loss, plus 7 dBd of antenna gain - net plus 2.8 dB, so ERP = 150 x 10^0.28 = 150 x 1.905, about 286 watts (adding the losses instead lands on the 469-watt distractor). Section 2 sets the two gain rulers side by side: the hypothetical isotropic radiator (0 dBi, equal in all directions) and the half-wave dipole (2.15 dBi = 0 dBd), so gain in dBd = gain in dBi minus 2.15 - 6 dBi is 3.85 dBd (E9A12). Section 3 runs two more pool chains: E9A06's 200 watts with minus 4, minus 3.2, minus 0.8 dB and plus 10 dBd nets plus 2 dB for about 317 W ERP (the 2,000-watt choice treats 10 dB as a straight times-ten), and E9A07's 200 watts with minus 2, minus 2.8, minus 1.2 dB and plus 7 dBi nets plus 1 dB for about 252 W EIRP. The reference decides the name: dBd gives ERP, dBi gives EIRP.
spoken: The figure builds radiated-power math as a chain. Four boxes - transmitter 150 watts, feed line minus 2 dB, duplexer minus 2.2 dB, antenna plus 7 dBd - run into a result bar: net plus 2.8 dB, so ERP is 150 times 10 to the 0.28, about 286 watts. Then the two gain rulers: an isotropic point source inside a dashed circle, 0 dBi, and a half-wave dipole with its figure-eight, 2.15 dBi or 0 dBd - gain in dBd equals gain in dBi minus 2.15, so 6 dBi is 3.85 dBd. Finally two compact chains from the pool: 200 watts through minus 4, minus 3.2, and minus 0.8 dB with a plus-10-dBd antenna nets plus 2 dB, about 317 watts ERP; and 200 watts through minus 2, minus 2.8, and minus 1.2 dB with a plus-7-dBi antenna nets plus 1 dB, about 252 watts EIRP. dBd pairs with ERP, dBi with EIRP.
